protocolBuilder.anonymisation.passphrase.description: Button that confirms switching off the passphrase rules and discarding them.

protocolBuilder.anonymisation.passphrase.defaultMessage: The lengths you set will be discarded, and participants will be able to choose any passphrase.
protocolBuilder.anonymisation.passphrase.description: Body of the confirmation shown before the passphrase rules are switched off, saying what is lost. The passphrase protects the answers the participant gives on this stage.
Title of the confirmation shown before a researcher switches off the requirements a participant’s passphrase has to meet. Switching them off discards them, which is why it is confirmed.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.addRowTitle.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to add a row to a list, where the list has offered no title of its own. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.addSubmit.description: Button that commits the dialog a researcher has filled in for a NEW row of a list. The same dialog says Save when it is editing a row that already exists.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.editRow.description: Accessible name of the button that opens one row of a list in its editing dialog. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.emptyState.defaultMessage: No items have been created yet.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.emptyState.description: Shown in place of the rows when a list has none, and the list’s caller has offered no wording of its own.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.itemNoun.description: Generic noun for one row of an editable list in a stage editor, used where the list has no more specific word for its rows. Interpolated mid-sentence into things said ABOUT a row ("Remove this item?", "This item was not saved."), so it is lower case and singular.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.listDisabledR.defaultMessage: This list is not accepting changes at the moment, so this {itemLabel} was not saved. Copy anything you want to keep, then try again once the list can be edited.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.listDisabledR.description: Shown above the fields of a row editor when the list itself has stopped accepting changes — because something else on the stage that it depends on is no longer chosen — so the row could not be saved. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows: "prompt", "option", "item".

protocolBuilder.arrayField.readOnlyRefus.defaultMessage: This stage is read-only, so this {itemLabel} was not saved. Take over editing and try again.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.readOnlyRefus.description: Shown to a researcher whose edit to one row of a list was refused because they no longer hold the right to edit the stage (one step of an interview). itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language. Taking over editing is an action offered elsewhere in the host application.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.removalUnavai.defaultMessage: This list stopped accepting changes while you were confirming, so this {itemLabel} was not removed. Remove it again once the list can be edited.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.removalUnavai.description: Shown inside a removal confirmation when the list stopped accepting changes while the researcher was reading it, so nothing was deleted. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.removeRow.description: Action that deletes one row of a list — the accessible name of the button on the row, and the confirm button of the confirmation it raises. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.removeRowDesc.defaultMessage: This {itemLabel} will be removed from the list.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.removeRowDesc.description: Body of the confirmation raised when a researcher deletes one row of a list. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.removeRowTitl.description: Title of the confirmation raised when a researcher deletes one row of a list. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.reorderRow.description: Accessible name of the handle that drags one row of a list into a different position. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language; position is the row’s own place in the list, counting from one; count is how many rows the list holds.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.rowEditorFail.defaultMessage: This editor could not be shown, so there is nothing to fill in here. Close it and try again. If it keeps happening, the problem is in this interface’s editor rather than in your protocol.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.rowEditorFail.description: Shown in place of the fields of a row-editing dialog when the interface’s own editor code threw while rendering. Says the fault is in the software rather than in anything the researcher wrote, so they do not go looking for a mistake in their protocol.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.rowRemovedRef.defaultMessage: This {itemLabel} was removed while your changes were being saved, so there is nothing left to save them to. Copy anything you want to keep, then cancel and add a new {itemLabel}.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.rowRemovedRef.description: Shown to a researcher whose edit to one row of a list was saved after that row had already been deleted. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows — "prompt", "option", "item" — already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.rowReplacedRe.defaultMessage: This {itemLabel} was replaced while you were confirming, so nothing was removed. Check the list and remove it again if you still want to.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.rowReplacedRe.description: Shown inside a removal confirmation when the row it was opened on has been replaced by a different one while the researcher was reading it, so nothing was deleted. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows — "prompt", "option", "item" — already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.rowUnresolved.defaultMessage: This list changed while you were editing, so this {itemLabel} could not be matched to a row in it and nothing was saved. Copy anything you want to keep, then check the list and make the change again.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.rowUnresolved.description: Shown to a researcher whose edit could not be matched to any one row of the list, because the list moved while they were editing. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.saveRefused.defaultMessage: This {itemLabel} could not be saved. Check your changes and try again.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.saveRefused.description: Shown above the fields of a row editor when saving was refused for a reason that gave no explanation of its own. The last resort. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows.

protocolBuilder.attributeCodebookControl.defaultMessage: An attribute participants choose an answer from needs at least two values, so it is created together with them.
protocolBuilder.attributeCodebookControl.description: Shown above the buttons when the researcher is inventing an attribute whose answers come from a list, explaining why they are sent to the codebook editor rather than being asked for a name here.

protocolBuilder.attributeCodebookControl.defaultMessage: Create this attribute and its values
protocolBuilder.attributeCodebookControl.description: Button that opens the codebook editor for inventing an attribute whose answers are chosen from a list, together with that list. Also the title of the dialog it opens. An attribute is one thing an interview records about a network member.
The same button for a yes/no attribute, whose two stored values are fixed and whose WORDS are what a researcher writes — so this says labels rather than values. Also the title of the dialog it opens.
The same button for an attribute whose answer is not chosen from a list — a date between two bounds, a position on a scale. Also the title of the dialog it opens.
Button that opens the codebook editor for the rules a participant’s answer has to satisfy. Also the title of the dialog it opens.
Button that opens the codebook editor for the list of answers a participant chooses between. Also the title of the dialog it opens.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.createDe.description: What the change is called in the record a host keeps of protocol edits, and in any undo history it offers. name is the attribute name the researcher typed.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.createVa.defaultMessage: This attribute could not be created, so nothing was changed. Try again.
protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.createVa.description: Refusal shown on the attribute control of a stage editor when inventing a new attribute (a codebook variable) failed for a reason with no explanation of its own.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.missingT.defaultMessage: This type is no longer in the codebook, so an attribute cannot be added to it.
protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.missingT.description: Refusal shown when the node or edge type the stage works with has been deleted from the codebook — the protocol’s definition of what an interview records — while the researcher was editing.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.missingV.defaultMessage: This attribute is no longer in the codebook. Choose another one.
protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.missingV.description: Refusal shown on the attribute control of a stage editor when the attribute a row names has been deleted from the codebook while the researcher was editing.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.nameTake.defaultMessage: An attribute with this name already exists here. Choose another name.
protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.nameTake.description: Refusal shown under the name field when another attribute of the same type is already called that.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.newVaria.defaultMessage: Not a valid attribute name. Only letters, numbers and the symbols ._-: are supported
protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.newVaria.description: Refusal shown under the name field of a stage editor when the name typed for a new attribute holds characters the export formats cannot carry. The listed symbols are literal characters and must not be translated. Said in the same words as the row-cell rule that judges an attribute name as it is typed.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.noSubjec.defaultMessage: Choose what this stage works with before creating an attribute.
protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.noSubjec.description: Refusal shown when a researcher tries to invent an attribute before choosing which node or edge type the stage (one step of an interview) is about, so there is no codebook section to add it to.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.setCompo.description: What the change is called in the record a host keeps of protocol edits, and in any undo history it offers. name is the attribute’s researcher-facing name.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.setCompo.defaultMessage: This attribute’s input control could not be changed, so nothing was changed. Try again.
protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.setCompo.description: Refusal shown on the input-control dropdown of a stage editor when recording which control an attribute is collected with failed for a reason with no explanation of its own.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.unsuppor.defaultMessage: This attribute cannot be collected with that input control.
protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.unsuppor.description: Refusal shown on the input-control dropdown when the control chosen cannot collect the kind of answer this attribute holds.

protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.boolean.description: Label of the field holding the words on one of the two answers a yes/no attribute offers. records says which of the two stored values this answer records; “true” and “false” are the literal values the protocol stores and an export records, so they stay as they are.

protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.boolean.defaultMessage: {records, select, true {Style “true” as negative} other {Style “false” as negative}}
protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.boolean.description: Label of the switch that draws one of the two answers of a yes/no attribute in red when a participant selects it. records says which of the two stored values this answer records; “true” and “false” are the literal values the protocol stores and stay as they are.

protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.repeate.defaultMessage: Give this answer different words: two buttons saying the same thing cannot be told apart.
protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.repeate.description: Refusal shown under the second of the two answers of a yes/no attribute when both have been given the same words, which leaves the participant two buttons they cannot tell apart.

protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.unnamed.defaultMessage: Write what this answer says, or clear both to offer Yes and No.
protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.unnamed.description: Refusal shown under one of the two answers of a yes/no attribute when it has been left blank while the other is written. Clearing both is a real answer: an attribute that names neither is offered to the participant as Yes and No.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.compound.defaultMessage: Another change to the codebook is still being saved. Wait for it to finish, then save this one.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.compound.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when a previous change to the codebook — the protocol’s definition of what an interview records — has not finished saving.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.heldBy.defaultMessage: {holder} is currently editing a section needed for this change.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.heldBy.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when a named collaborator is editing part of the protocol the change needs. holder is that person’s display name, which the host supplies.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.heldBySo.defaultMessage: A section needed for this change is currently being edited.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.heldBySo.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when part of the protocol the change needs is being edited by somebody the host would not name.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.hostErro.defaultMessage: The protocol would not be valid with this change, so nothing was saved. Adjust this type and try again, or close this and come back once the rest of the stage is filled in.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.hostErro.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when the change would leave the whole protocol invalid — usually because the stage being configured is not finished yet. A stage is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.invalidR.defaultMessage: This change could not be sent, and nothing was saved. Close this editor and try again.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.invalidR.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when the change could not be sent for saving at all.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.invalidR.defaultMessage: The protocol came back in a state this editor cannot read, so nothing here has been kept. Reload the protocol before making this change.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.invalidR.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when what came back after saving was not something the editor could read.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.leaseLos.defaultMessage: You are no longer the editor of this stage, so nothing was saved. Take over editing and try again.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.leaseLos.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when the researcher no longer holds the right to edit this stage. Taking over editing is an action offered elsewhere in the host application.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.pendingC.defaultMessage: A file you added is still waiting to be saved with this stage. Save the stage first, then make this change.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.pendingC.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when the stage still holds an imported file that has not been saved, which has to land before the codebook can change.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.staleBas.defaultMessage: Someone else changed this while you were editing it, so nothing was saved. Close and reopen this editor to load their version, then make your change again.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.staleBas.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when a collaborator changed the same thing while this editor was open.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.staleEpo.defaultMessage: Editing access changed while this was being saved, so nothing was saved. Try again.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.staleEpo.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when who holds the right to edit changed midway through saving.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.staleRes.defaultMessage: A newer version of the protocol is already open, so this change was not applied. Try again.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.staleRes.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when a newer version of the protocol had already been loaded by the time the change came back.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.unavaila.defaultMessage: This editor cannot change the codebook right now. Reload the protocol and try again.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.unavaila.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when the host cannot accept codebook changes at all just now.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.unexplai.defaultMessage: This change could not be saved, and nothing was altered. Wait a moment and try again.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.unexplai.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when saving threw with no explanation a researcher could act on. The last resort.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.audioHint.defaultMessage: The audio the participant can play when they reach this block.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.audioHint.description: Guidance under the file picker of a block that plays an audio recording.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.audioRequir.defaultMessage: Choose the audio file this block plays.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.audioRequir.description: Refusal shown under the file picker of an audio block when nothing has been chosen.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.contentLabe.description: Label of the control holding what one piece of a page actually shows, whichever kind it is.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.imageHint.defaultMessage: The image the participant sees when they reach this block.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.imageHint.description: Guidance under the file picker of a block that shows a picture.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.imageRequir.defaultMessage: Choose the image this block shows.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.imageRequir.description: Refusal shown under the file picker of a picture block when nothing has been chosen.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindAudio.description: Choice offered for what one piece of a page holds: an audio recording.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindChanged.defaultMessage: Content type changed to {kind}. Nothing has been entered for {kind} yet.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindChanged.description: Announcement made when a researcher changes what kind of thing one piece of a page holds and neither the old nor the new kind has anything in it. kind is the new choice, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindChanged.defaultMessage: Content type changed to {kind}. The content you entered for the previous type is kept, and returns if you change back to it.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindChanged.description: Announcement made when a researcher changes what kind of thing one piece of a page holds, away from a kind they had filled in, which is kept rather than thrown away. kind is the new choice, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindChanged.defaultMessage: Content type changed to {kind}. The content you entered for {kind} earlier has been restored.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindChanged.description: Announcement made when a researcher changes what kind of thing one piece of a page holds, back to a kind they had already filled in, so their earlier answer comes back. kind is that choice, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindChosen.defaultMessage: Content type set to {kind}. A content field for it has been added below.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindChosen.description: Announcement made when a researcher first says what kind of thing one piece of a page holds, which mounts a control for it. kind is that choice — Image, Video, Audio, Text — already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindHint.defaultMessage: Choose what this block shows the participant.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindImage.description: Choice offered for what one piece of a page holds: a picture.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindLabel.description: Label of the control choosing what kind of thing one piece of a page holds — a picture, a video, an audio recording, prose.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindRequire.defaultMessage: Choose what kind of content this block holds.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindRequire.description: Refusal shown under the content-type control when the researcher has chosen nothing.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindText.description: Choice offered for what one piece of a page holds: prose the participant reads.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindVideo.description: Choice offered for what one piece of a page holds: a video.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.missingReso.defaultMessage: This block’s resource is no longer in this protocol. Choose a content type above to replace it.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.missingReso.description: Warning body shown when a piece of a page points at a file that has been deleted from the protocol, so it needs replacing.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.previewEmpt.defaultMessage: This block has no content yet.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.previewEmpt.description: Shown in the collapsed row of a page’s list of blocks when the researcher has not yet said what that piece of the page holds.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.previewUnus.defaultMessage: This block’s resource is not in this protocol, or is not something a page can show.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.previewUnus.description: Shown in the collapsed row of a page’s list of blocks when that piece points at a file the protocol no longer holds, or at one a page cannot present — a roster of people, a map layer, a key.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sectionDesc.defaultMessage: Choose what kind of content this block holds, and provide the content itself.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sectionTitl.description: Heading of the dialog where a researcher says what one piece of a page holds and provides it.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sizeFull.description: Choice offered for how tall a picture or video on a page is drawn: however tall it naturally is, unconstrained.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sizeHint.defaultMessage: Optionally constrain the height of this block. Full size lets it show at its natural height.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sizeHint.description: Guidance under the display-size control. "Full size" is the wording of the unconstrained choice it offers.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sizeLabel.description: Label of the control constraining how tall a picture or video is drawn on a page.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sizeLarge.description: Choice offered for how tall a picture or video on a page is drawn.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sizeMedium.description: Choice offered for how tall a picture or video on a page is drawn.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sizeSmall.description: Choice offered for how tall a picture or video on a page is drawn.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.textHint.defaultMessage: What the participant reads when they reach this block. Supports markdown formatting.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.textHint.description: Guidance under the control holding the prose of a text block. Markdown is the name of the formatting syntax and is not translated.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.textPlaceho.defaultMessage: Enter the text for this block...
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.textPlaceho.description: Placeholder shown in the empty prose control of a text block. The trailing dots are an ellipsis written as three full stops.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.textRequire.defaultMessage: Write the text this block shows.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.textRequire.description: Refusal shown under the prose control of a text block when it has been left empty.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.unpresentab.defaultMessage: This block’s resource is not an image, audio or video file, so this block cannot show it. Choose a content type above to replace it.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.unpresentab.description: Warning body shown when a piece of a page points at a file that IS in the protocol but is not something a page can present — a roster of people, a map layer, a key. Distinct from a deleted file, because there is nothing missing to go looking for.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.unusableTit.description: Warning heading shown when a piece of a page points at a file the page cannot present.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.videoHint.defaultMessage: The video the participant can play when they reach this block.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.videoHint.description: Guidance under the file picker of a block that plays a video.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.videoRequir.defaultMessage: Choose the video this block plays.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.videoRequir.description: Refusal shown under the file picker of a video block when nothing has been chosen.

protocolBuilder.formFields.addLabel.description: Button that opens the dialog for adding one more question to a form. Whole rather than a generic "Add", because a stage editor shows several lists at once.

protocolBuilder.formFields.addTitle.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to add one more question to a form.

protocolBuilder.formFields.atLeastOne.defaultMessage: Add at least one field. A form with no fields collects nothing.
protocolBuilder.formFields.atLeastOne.description: Refusal shown above a form’s list of fields when a researcher saves a form that asks nothing. A field is one question bound to one attribute of a network member.

protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeEmpt.defaultMessage: Every attribute of this type is already collected or written elsewhere. Create a new one instead.
protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeEmpt.description: Shown in place of the attribute list when every attribute of this node or edge type is either already collected by another field of the same form, or written somewhere the protocol will not let a form field also write.

protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeHint.defaultMessage: The codebook attribute this field’s answer is stored in.
protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeHint.description: Guidance under the attribute control. The codebook is the protocol’s definition of what an interview records.

protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeLabe.description: Label of the control choosing which attribute this question’s answer is recorded under. The same word as the section heading above it, and translated once for each.

protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeRequ.defaultMessage: Choose the attribute this field collects.
protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeRequ.description: Refusal shown under the attribute control when nothing has been chosen.

protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeSect.defaultMessage: Choose the attribute this field collects, or create one for it.

protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeSect.description: Heading of the half of the field dialog that says which attribute this question’s answer is recorded under.

protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeTake.defaultMessage: Another field in this form already collects this attribute. Choose a different one, or edit that field instead.
protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeTake.description: Refusal shown under the attribute control when a sibling field of the same form already records its answer under the attribute just chosen.

protocolBuilder.formFields.componentHint.defaultMessage: What the participant uses to answer. Changing it changes how this attribute is collected everywhere.
protocolBuilder.formFields.componentHint.description: Guidance under the input-control field, warning that the control belongs to the attribute rather than to this one question.

protocolBuilder.formFields.componentLabe.description: Label of the control choosing what the participant uses to answer — a text box, a slider, a set of buttons.

protocolBuilder.formFields.componentRequ.defaultMessage: Choose how the participant answers this field.
protocolBuilder.formFields.componentRequ.description: Refusal shown under the input-control field when nothing has been chosen.

protocolBuilder.formFields.createNewOpti.description: The last choice in the attribute list, which stands for an attribute that does not exist yet and asks the researcher to name one. The trailing character is an ellipsis.

protocolBuilder.formFields.createWithVal.defaultMessage: Create this attribute and the values it offers before adding the field that collects it.
protocolBuilder.formFields.createWithVal.description: Refusal shown under the kind-of-answer control when a researcher tries to invent an attribute whose answers come from a list, which cannot be made from a name and a kind alone.

protocolBuilder.formFields.description.defaultMessage: Choose the attributes this form collects, and write the question the participant answers for each.

protocolBuilder.formFields.duplicateFiel.defaultMessage: Two fields collect the same attribute. Each attribute may be collected once per form.
protocolBuilder.formFields.duplicateFiel.description: Refusal shown above a form’s list of fields when two of them record their answers under the same attribute, which would leave only one of the answers.

protocolBuilder.formFields.editTitle.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to change a question a form already asks.

protocolBuilder.formFields.emptyState.defaultMessage: No fields yet. Create one to say what this form collects.
protocolBuilder.formFields.emptyState.description: Shown in place of the list of form fields while a form asks nothing yet.

protocolBuilder.formFields.fieldHint.defaultMessage: The participant answers these one after another, in this order. Add at least one.
protocolBuilder.formFields.fieldHint.description: Guidance under the list of form fields.

protocolBuilder.formFields.fieldLabel.description: Label of the ordered list of questions a form asks.

protocolBuilder.formFields.formTitleHint.defaultMessage: Shown above the form. Use a short phrase describing what it collects, such as "Add a person".
protocolBuilder.formFields.formTitleHint.description: Guidance under the form-title field. The quoted phrase is an example a researcher might write, and should be translated as such.

protocolBuilder.formFields.formTitleLabe.description: Label of the field holding the heading shown above the form a participant fills in.

protocolBuilder.formFields.formTitlePlac.description: Example form title shown in the empty field. An example a researcher might write, not a value that is stored.

protocolBuilder.formFields.formTitleRequ.description: Refusal shown under the form-title field when it has been left empty.

protocolBuilder.formFields.hintHint.defaultMessage: Optional guidance shown below the question, for a field participants may find ambiguous.

protocolBuilder.formFields.hintLabel.description: Label of the optional field holding extra guidance shown to the participant under the question.

protocolBuilder.formFields.hintPlacehold.description: Example hint shown in the empty hint-text field. An example a researcher might write, not a value that is stored.

protocolBuilder.formFields.incompleteFie.defaultMessage: Every field needs both an attribute and a question. Open the incomplete field and finish it.
protocolBuilder.formFields.incompleteFie.description: Refusal shown above a form’s list of fields when one of them names no attribute, or asks no question.

protocolBuilder.formFields.itemNoun.description: What one row of a form’s list of questions is called inside things said ABOUT it — "Edit field", "Remove this field?" — so it is lower case and singular.

protocolBuilder.formFields.newNameHint.defaultMessage: How this attribute is named in the codebook and in exported data.
protocolBuilder.formFields.newNameHint.description: Guidance under the new-attribute name field. The codebook is the protocol’s definition of what an interview records; exported data is the file a researcher analyses afterwards.

protocolBuilder.formFields.newNameLabel.description: Label of the field naming an attribute the researcher is inventing.

protocolBuilder.formFields.newNamePlaceh.description: Example attribute name shown in the empty field. An example a researcher might write, not a value that is stored.

protocolBuilder.formFields.newNameRequir.defaultMessage: Name the attribute this field collects.
protocolBuilder.formFields.newNameRequir.description: Refusal shown under the new-attribute name field when it has been left empty.

protocolBuilder.formFields.newTypeHint.defaultMessage: What this attribute holds. It cannot be changed once answers have been collected.

protocolBuilder.formFields.newTypeLabel.description: Label of the control choosing what sort of value a new attribute holds — text, a number, a date, a choice from a list.

protocolBuilder.formFields.newTypeRequir.defaultMessage: Choose what kind of answer this attribute holds.
protocolBuilder.formFields.newTypeRequir.description: Refusal shown under the kind-of-answer control when nothing has been chosen.

protocolBuilder.formFields.previewCollec.description: Shown in the collapsed row of a form’s list of questions, saying which attribute it records into and what kind of value that holds. name is the attribute’s researcher-facing name; type is a schema token such as text, number or ordinal, which is not translated.

protocolBuilder.formFields.previewMissin.defaultMessage: This attribute is no longer in the codebook.
protocolBuilder.formFields.previewMissin.description: Shown in the collapsed row of a form’s list of questions when the attribute it records into has been deleted from the codebook.

protocolBuilder.formFields.promptHint.defaultMessage: Shown to the participant above the control. Supports markdown formatting.
protocolBuilder.formFields.promptHint.description: Guidance under the question-text field. Markdown is the name of the formatting syntax and is not translated.

protocolBuilder.formFields.promptLabel.description: Label of the field holding what the participant is asked for this one answer.

protocolBuilder.formFields.promptPlaceho.description: Example question shown in the empty question-text field. An example a researcher might write, not a value that is stored.

protocolBuilder.formFields.promptRequire.defaultMessage: Write the question this field asks.
protocolBuilder.formFields.promptRequire.description: Refusal shown under the question-text field when it has been left empty.

protocolBuilder.formFields.questionSecti.defaultMessage: Write what the participant is asked, and how much help they are given.

protocolBuilder.interface.geospatial.description: Researcher-facing interface name. Interface for locating network members on a map. Not a protocol-authored stage label.

protocolBuilder.introduction.headingPlac.description: Placeholder shown in the empty introduction-heading field. The trailing dots are an ellipsis written as three full stops.

protocolBuilder.introduction.textLabel.description: Label of the field holding the prose a participant reads before this step of the interview begins.

protocolBuilder.introduction.textPlaceho.description: Placeholder shown in the empty introduction-text field. The trailing dots are an ellipsis written as three full stops.

protocolBuilder.introduction.title.description: Heading of the section where a researcher writes what a participant reads before this step of the interview begins.

protocolBuilder.multiSelect.emptyState.description: Shown in place of the rows when a list has none, and the list’s caller has offered no wording of its own.

protocolBuilder.multiSelect.incompleteRo.defaultMessage: Every row needs a value in each column.
protocolBuilder.multiSelect.incompleteRo.description: Shown above a list of rows in a stage editor when the researcher tries to save with a row that has an empty cell in it. Each row here is a set of dropdowns filled in together — a sort rule, a display property.

protocolBuilder.multiSelect.removeItem.description: Action that deletes one row of a list. Used as the button on the row, as the title of the confirmation it raises, and as that confirmation’s own confirm button.

protocolBuilder.multiSelect.removeItemDe.defaultMessage: Are you sure you want to remove this item?
protocolBuilder.multiSelect.removeItemDe.description: Body of the confirmation raised when a researcher deletes one row of a list.

protocolBuilder.multiSelect.reorderItem.description: Accessible name of the handle that drags one row of a list into a different position. position is the row’s own place in the list, counting from one; count is how many rows the list holds.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.atRisk.defaultMessage: Choose whether the pedigree also shows inferred risk alongside recorded status.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.atRisk.description: Description of the at-risk statuses section. Inferred risk is worked out from the family structure; recorded status is what someone actually entered. A pedigree is a family tree.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.atRisk.defaultMessage: Off by default. At-risk symbols are inferred rather than observed, and are intended for clinician-directed use.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.atRisk.description: Guidance under the at-risk switch, saying in one line why it starts off. The prose below the switch says the same thing at length.
Label of the switch turning inferred risk on. The bracketed words name what these are called on the family tree itself.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.atRisk.defaultMessage: Two rules constrain how risk travels through a family. Only biological and donor relationships pass conditions on; social, adoptive, surrogate and partner links do not. And where a person’s biological sex is not known, sex-linked inheritance through that person is left uncertain rather than guessed.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.atRisk.description: Says the two limits on inference. The named relationship kinds — biological, donor, social, adoptive, surrogate, partner — are the ones a Family Pedigree stage records, so they should read the same here as they do there.
Heading over the paragraphs explaining where an inferred at-risk status comes from.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.atRisk.defaultMessage: At-risk statuses are not observed or diagnosed. They are inferred from the family structure together with each condition’s inheritance pattern — the child of a parent affected by a dominant condition is shown as may develop it, and the child of two carriers of a recessive condition as may carry it.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.atRisk.description: Says what an at-risk status is worked out from, with one example of each kind. The <em> tags mark the two phrases drawn from standard pedigree nomenclature; a carrier holds a condition without developing it.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.atRisk.defaultMessage: When this is on, the pedigree also shows a person who may develop a condition or may carry it. These are drawn as the usual status symbol with a question mark (“?”) added. A solid, filled symbol always means a clinically affected individual, so at-risk relatives always appear as unfilled symbols marked with a “?”.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.atRisk.description: First paragraph of the prose explaining at-risk statuses to a researcher. The <em> tags mark the three phrases drawn from standard pedigree nomenclature; the quoted question mark is the symbol drawn on the family tree, so it stays a question mark whatever quotation marks the language uses around it.
Heading of the section deciding whether the family tree also marks people who MIGHT develop or carry a condition, as well as those recorded as having it.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.atRisk.defaultMessage: At-risk symbols are a strong visual signal that can be read as established fact rather than inferred risk. They are intended for clinician-directed use, where the result is interpreted in context. Standard pedigree nomenclature deliberately does not encode probabilistic risk, so leave this off unless a clinician is guiding interpretation.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.atRisk.description: The argument for leaving inferred risk off. The <strong> tag marks the condition under which showing it is appropriate: a clinician deciding to, and reading the result. "Standard pedigree nomenclature" is the published convention for drawing family trees in clinical genetics.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.atRisk.defaultMessage: Why this is off by default
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.atRisk.description: Heading over the paragraph explaining why inferred risk is not shown unless a researcher asks for it.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: The colour this disease is drawn in on the pedigree.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Guidance under the disease-colour control. A pedigree is a family tree.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Colour
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Label of the control choosing which colour one condition is drawn in on the family tree.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Colour {position}
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: How one entry of the disease-colour list is named. The palette’s colours have no names of their own — they are the study’s own theme colours — so they are counted instead. position identifies which one, counting from 1.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Select a colour...
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Placeholder shown in the disease-colour control while no colour has been chosen. The trailing dots are an ellipsis written as three full stops.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Choose a colour for this disease.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Refusal shown under the disease-colour control when the researcher saves the dialog without choosing one.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Create a boolean attribute recording who is affected by this disease
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Says what the attribute being created is for, inside the dialog that creates it. Boolean is a yes/no attribute. No full stop, because it reads as a caption above the form rather than as a sentence of prose.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Create a new affected-status attribute
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Button inside the disease dialog that adds a new yes/no field to the source pedigree’s own family members, for a condition the study does not record yet.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: How the disease is passed on. Mendelian patterns let the pedigree infer carrier and at-risk statuses from biological relationships and recorded sex; multifactorial and unknown show affected status only.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Guidance under the inheritance-pattern control. "Mendelian" describes the classical single-gene patterns; a carrier holds a condition without developing it; "multifactorial" and "unknown" are two of the choices in the list, and are written here in lower case because they are named inside a sentence.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Inheritance pattern
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Label of the control choosing how one condition travels from parent to child.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Select an inheritance pattern...
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Placeholder shown in the inheritance-pattern control while none has been chosen. The trailing dots are an ellipsis written as three full stops.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Choose how this disease is inherited.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Refusal shown under the inheritance-pattern control when the researcher saves the dialog without choosing one.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Shown to the participant in the pedigree's key, so it should be a name they recognise.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Guidance under the disease-name field. The key is the legend drawn beside the family tree, naming what each colour means.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Disease name
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Label of the field holding what one condition is called in the key the participant reads.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Enter a name for this disease...
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Placeholder shown in the empty disease-name field. The trailing dots are an ellipsis written as three full stops.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Give this disease a name.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Refusal shown under the disease-name field when the researcher saves the dialog having left it empty.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: disease
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: What one row of the disease list is called inside things said ABOUT it — "Edit disease", "Remove this disease?" — so it is lower case and singular. A disease here is a condition the stage draws on the family tree.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Unnamed disease
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Stands in for the name in the collapsed row of the disease list while the researcher has not written one, so the row can still be told apart and opened.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: The source pedigree has no boolean attributes a disease can be mapped to.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Said in place of the affected-status list when the family collected by the source stage records nothing a disease could be read from.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: The boolean attribute of the source pedigree that records who is affected.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Guidance under the affected-status control. Boolean is a yes/no attribute; the source pedigree is the earlier stage that collected the family.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Affected-status attribute
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Label of the control choosing which recorded field of a family member says whether they have this condition. An attribute is one field of data recorded about a person.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Choose the attribute that records who is affected.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Refusal shown under the affected-status control when the researcher saves the dialog without choosing one.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Create new disease
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Button that opens the dialog for describing one more condition. Whole rather than a generic "Add", because a stage editor shows several lists at once and they would otherwise be indistinguishable to anyone navigating by a list of buttons.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Create disease
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to describe one more condition.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Add at least one disease. A narrative pedigree with none shows the participant an unmarked family.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Refusal shown above the disease list when a researcher saves a stage that would draw nothing. "Narrative pedigree" is the name of this kind of interview step.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Define the conditions this stage draws on the family, and how each is inherited.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Description of the diseases section. A stage is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Another disease already uses this name. Give this one a name participants can tell apart.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Refusal shown under the name control in the disease dialog when a sibling disease already carries that name. The name is what the participant reads in the key beside the family tree, so two the same are indistinguishable on screen.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: This attribute is already mapped by another disease. Choose a different one, or edit the existing disease instead.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Refusal shown under the attribute control in the disease dialog when a sibling disease already records who is affected under the attribute just chosen. An attribute is one field of data recorded about a person.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Edit disease
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to change a condition they have already described.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: No diseases yet. Create one to mark who in the family is affected.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Shown in place of the disease list while this stage would draw nothing on the family.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Each disease maps one boolean attribute of the source pedigree's family members. Drag to reorder them in the key.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Guidance under the list of diseases. An attribute is one field of data recorded about a person; boolean is a yes/no attribute; the key is the legend the participant reads beside the family tree.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Diseases
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Label of the list of conditions inside the diseases section. The same word as the section heading, and translated once for each: the heading names the part of the stage, and this names the control.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Diseases
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Heading of the section listing the conditions this step of the interview draws onto the family tree.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.defaultMessage: Choose the Family Pedigree stage this one reads before defining its diseases.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.diseas.description: Said instead of the diseases section’s description while no source stage has been chosen, so there is no family and no set of attributes to describe a disease against.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.inheri.description: One choice in the inheritance-pattern list: a condition on a non-sex chromosome that one affected parent is enough to pass on. Standard clinical genetics terminology.
One choice in the inheritance-pattern list: a condition on a non-sex chromosome that needs a copy from both parents. Standard clinical genetics terminology.
One choice in the inheritance-pattern list: a condition passed on through the mother’s mitochondria. Standard clinical genetics terminology.
One choice in the inheritance-pattern list: a condition arising from several genes and the environment together, so nothing can be inferred from the family tree alone.
One choice in the inheritance-pattern list, said of the condition rather than of the researcher: how it is inherited has not been established, so only recorded status is drawn.
One choice in the inheritance-pattern list: a dominant condition carried on the X chromosome. Standard clinical genetics terminology; "X" is the chromosome’s letter and is not translated.
One choice in the inheritance-pattern list: a recessive condition carried on the X chromosome. Standard clinical genetics terminology; "X" is the chromosome’s letter and is not translated.
One choice in the inheritance-pattern list: a condition carried on the Y chromosome. Standard clinical genetics terminology; "Y" is the chromosome’s letter and is not translated.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.source.defaultMessage: The Family Pedigree stage this one reads now runs after it, so the family would still be empty. Move it earlier in the interview, or choose a pedigree that runs before this stage.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.source.description: Shown when the stage this one draws its family from has been moved to run later in the interview, so the participant would not have built the family yet.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.source.defaultMessage: Choose the Family Pedigree stage whose family this stage visualises.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.source.description: Description of the pedigree-source section. "Family Pedigree" is the name of another kind of interview step, the one in which the participant builds their family tree; a stage is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.source.defaultMessage: This interview has no Family Pedigree stage before this one. Add one, or move this stage later, before configuring it.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.source.description: Body of the notice shown in place of the source-stage control when nothing in the interview qualifies. "Family Pedigree" names the kind of interview step that collects a family tree.
Heading of the notice shown in place of the source-stage control when the interview holds no family tree this stage could draw.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.source.defaultMessage: Only Family Pedigree stages that run before this one are listed: the family has to be drawn before it can be shown.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.source.description: Guidance under the source-stage control, explaining why the list is shorter than the interview. "Family Pedigree" names another kind of interview step; a stage is one step of an interview.
Label of the control naming which earlier step of the interview collected the family this one draws on.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.source.defaultMessage: The Family Pedigree stage this one reads is no longer part of the interview. Choose another one, or restore it, before this stage can be saved.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.source.description: Shown when the stage this one draws its family from has been deleted or dropped out of the interview — usually by a collaborator, while this editor was open.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.source.defaultMessage: The stage this one reads is no longer a Family Pedigree, so there is no family for it to visualise. Choose a Family Pedigree stage instead.
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.source.description: Shown when the stage this one draws its family from has been changed to a different kind of interview step, so it no longer collects a family tree.
Placeholder shown in the source-stage control while no stage has been chosen. The trailing dots are an ellipsis written as three full stops.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.source.defaultMessage: This stage has no family to show
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.source.description: Heading of the warning shown when the stage this one was pointed at can no longer be used. The sentence under it says which of the three things went wrong.
Heading of the section where a researcher chooses which earlier step of the interview collected the family this step draws on. A pedigree is a family tree.

protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.source.defaultMessage: {stageId} — this stage can no longer be used
protocolBuilder.narrativePedigree.source.description: How the stored choice is labelled inside the source-stage list once it can no longer be used, so the researcher can still see what this stage points at. stageId is the missing stage’s identifier — not a name a person wrote, because there is no longer a stage to read a name from.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.background.defaultMessage: The rings drawn behind the nodes. Participants often use them to place people closer to or further from themselves.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.background.description: Label of the box holding how many rings are drawn behind the nodes.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.background.defaultMessage: The conventional sociogram background: rings the participant places nodes within.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.background.description: Says what a concentric-circles background is for. A sociogram is the canvas interface where a participant arranges the people in their network.
Name of the background made of rings drawn one inside another. Offered as one of two cards; the sentence under it is backgroundCirclesOptionDescription.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.background.defaultMessage: Enter the number of circles as a whole number of zero or more.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.background.description: Refusal shown under the number-of-circles box when it holds something that is not a whole number of zero or more. Zero is allowed: it is a canvas with no rings drawn on it.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.background.defaultMessage: Choose what the participant sees behind the nodes on this canvas.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.background.description: Description of the background section on an interface whose canvas can only draw concentric circles, so there is no choice of background kind to make.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.background.defaultMessage: Choose what the participant sees behind the nodes on this canvas: concentric circles, or a picture of your own.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.background.description: Description of the background section on an interface whose canvas can also draw an image, where the researcher chooses between the two kinds of background.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.background.defaultMessage: Scaled to fill the canvas. A responsive SVG keeps its labels readable in both portrait and landscape.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.background.description: Guidance under the background-image picker. SVG is a file format name and is not translated.
Label of the control choosing which protocol resource is drawn behind the nodes.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.background.defaultMessage: A picture of your own — a map, a floor plan, a diagram — filling the canvas.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.background.description: Says what an image background is for, with three examples of what researchers use. Addressed to the researcher.
Name of the background made of a picture the researcher supplies. Offered as one of two cards; the sentence under it is backgroundImageOptionDescription.
Label of the control choosing between the two kinds of background a canvas can have.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.background.defaultMessage: Gives the inner rings more room than the outer ones, so nodes placed near the centre overlap less.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.background.description: Label of the switch giving the rings nearest the centre more room than the outer ones.
Heading of the section deciding what is drawn behind the nodes on a canvas. Also names the section in the editor outline and to assistive technology.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.canvasInte.defaultMessage: Choose what the participant may do to the picture while they tell their story.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.canvasInte.description: Description of the canvas-interaction section on a narrative stage, where the participant is shown the network they have already built and asked to talk about it. The sociogram’s wording is sociogramCanvasInteractionDescription.
Heading of the section granting or withholding what the participant may do to the canvas. Also names the section in the editor outline and to assistive technology.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerAu.defaultMessage: Arranges the nodes by simulating attraction and repulsion. The participant can switch this off and on during the interview; this is only where it starts.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerAu.description: Guidance under the start-with-automatic-layout switch, saying that the researcher is choosing a starting point rather than taking the choice away from the participant.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerAu.defaultMessage: Start with automatic layout switched on
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerAu.description: Label of the switch deciding whether a Network Composer canvas is already arranging its nodes when the participant arrives.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerCr.defaultMessage: Create an attribute to store node positions, and use it on this stage
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerCr.description: Description at the top of the dialog for creating a layout attribute from a Network Composer stage. No full stop in the English: it is a subtitle rather than a sentence.
Button beside the composer position-attribute picker that adds a layout attribute to the codebook without leaving the stage. Also the title of the dialog it opens.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerEd.defaultMessage: Choose the kinds of connection the participant can draw between nodes on this canvas.
This protocol has no connection types yet. Create one to let the participant connect nodes.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerEd.description: Shown in place of the connection-types tick list when the protocol’s codebook defines no edge type at all.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerEd.defaultMessage: The participant can draw a connection of any kind you tick here. Leave them all unticked to build a network of nodes alone.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerEd.description: Guidance under the connection-types tick list. Addressed to the researcher; ticking nothing is a real answer rather than an unfinished one.
Label of the tick list choosing which edge types the stage draws.

Heading of the section deciding which kinds of relationship a participant may draw between nodes on a Network Composer canvas. Also names the section in the editor outline and to assistive technology.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerLa.defaultMessage: This type has no position attributes yet. Create one to store where the participant puts each node.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerLa.description: Shown in place of the composer position-attribute picker when the node type this stage is about has no layout attribute in the codebook. "This type" is that node type.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerLa.defaultMessage: The attribute that stores each node's position. Stages sharing an attribute carry the participant's placements between them.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerLa.description: Guidance under the composer position-attribute picker. A stage is one step of an interview.
Label of the picker naming the codebook attribute a Network Composer stage stores each node’s position in. A layout attribute holds a pair of coordinates.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerNo.defaultMessage: How the participant adds nodes to the canvas, where those nodes sit, and how they group them.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerNo.description: Heading of the section deciding what a participant can do with nodes on a Network Composer canvas. Also names the section in the editor outline and to assistive technology.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerNo.defaultMessage: Choose what this stage works with before configuring how its nodes behave.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.composerNo.description: Shown in place of the adding-and-arranging-nodes description while the researcher has not yet chosen which node type the stage is about, so every attribute picker in it would have nothing to offer.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.createEdge.defaultMessage: Create a connection type, and let the participant draw it on this stage
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.createEdge.description: Description at the top of the dialog for creating an edge type from a Network Composer stage. No full stop in the English: it is a subtitle rather than a sentence.
Button beside the connection-types tick list that adds an edge type to the protocol without leaving the stage. Also the title of the dialog it opens.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.createHull.defaultMessage: Create an attribute with a fixed set of values, and group nodes by it
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.createHull.description: Description at the top of the dialog for creating a categorical attribute from the grouping picker. No full stop in the English: it is a subtitle rather than a sentence.
Button beside the composer grouping-attribute picker that adds a categorical attribute to the codebook without leaving the stage. Also the title of the dialog it opens.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.createQuic.defaultMessage: Create a free-text attribute, and fill it in when a node is added
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.createQuic.description: Description at the top of the dialog for creating a text attribute from the quick-add picker. No full stop in the English: it is a subtitle rather than a sentence.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.createQuic.defaultMessage: Create a new attribute to fill in
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.createQuic.description: Button beside the quick-add attribute picker that adds a text attribute to the codebook without leaving the stage. Also the title of the dialog it opens.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.duplicateV.defaultMessage: Another field on this form already records this attribute. Choose a different one, or edit the existing field instead.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.duplicateV.description: Refusal shown under a composer form field’s attribute picker when a sibling field of the same form already records its answer under the attribute just chosen.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.edgeFormAd.defaultMessage: Create new attribute field for "{typeName}" connections
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.edgeFormAd.description: Button that opens the dialog for adding one more question to one connection type’s form. Names the type because a stage draws several kinds of connection and their lists sit one under another. typeName is the edge type’s researcher-facing name, shown inside straight double quotes.
Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to add one more question to one connection type’s form. typeName is the edge type’s researcher-facing name, shown inside straight double quotes.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.edgeFormEd.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to change a question one connection type’s form already asks. typeName is the edge type’s researcher-facing name, shown inside straight double quotes.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.edgeFormEm.defaultMessage: No attributes yet for this connection type. Create one to ask the participant something about each connection they draw.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.edgeFormEm.description: Shown in place of one connection type’s list of fields while its form asks nothing yet.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.edgeFormFi.description: What one row of a connection form’s list is called inside things said ABOUT it, so it is lower case and singular. A connection is an edge — a relationship drawn between two people in the network.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.edgeFormFi.defaultMessage: The participant answers these in the panel that opens when they select a connection of this kind. Drag to reorder them.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.edgeFormFi.description: Guidance under one connection form’s list of fields.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.edgeFormHe.description: Heading naming which connection type the form below it belongs to. typeName is the edge type’s researcher-facing name from the codebook, shown inside straight double quotes.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.edgeFormsD.defaultMessage: Optionally ask the participant more about each connection they draw. Each connection type is asked about separately, because each records its own attributes.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.edgeFormsT.description: Heading of the section holding one form per connection type the stage draws. Also names the section in the editor outline and to assistive technology.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.fieldParam.defaultMessage: These settings belong to this field rather than to the attribute, so the same attribute can be asked for differently on another form.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.fieldParam.description: Guidance under the settings block’s heading, explaining that these settings are saved with the stage rather than with the codebook attribute.
Heading of the block inside a composer form field’s dialog holding the settings the chosen input control takes — the two dates a date picker allows, the words at each end of a sliding scale.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.formFieldC.defaultMessage: How the participant answers. Only controls that can render this attribute are listed.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.formFieldC.description: Guidance under the input-control picker, saying why some controls are missing from it.
Label of the picker naming which on-screen control the participant answers this field with — a text box, a slider, a set of radio buttons.
Placeholder shown in the input-control picker before one is chosen. The trailing dots are an ellipsis written as three full stops.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.formFieldC.defaultMessage: Choose how the participant answers this field.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.formFieldC.description: Refusal shown under the input-control picker when the researcher saves a field without choosing one.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.formFieldE.description: Stands in for a field’s question in the collapsed row of a composer form’s field list while the researcher has neither written a question nor chosen an attribute to borrow a name from.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.formFieldH.defaultMessage: Shown under the question, for anything the participant might need explained. Optional.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.formFieldH.description: Guidance under the form field’s help-text box.
Label of the box holding an optional explanation shown under this field’s question.
Placeholder shown in the empty help-text box. The trailing dots are an ellipsis written as three full stops.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.formFieldQ.defaultMessage: What the participant is asked. Leave it empty to use the attribute's own name.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.formFieldQ.description: Guidance under the form field’s question box, saying what happens when it is left empty.
Label of the box holding the words the participant reads above this field.
Placeholder shown in the empty question box. The trailing dots are an ellipsis written as three full stops.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.formFieldR.description: Badge in the collapsed row of a composer form’s field list saying which codebook attribute that field writes to. attributeName is the attribute’s researcher-facing name, shown inside straight double quotes.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.formFieldV.defaultMessage: This type has no attributes a form can collect yet. Create one in the codebook to continue.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.formFieldV.description: Shown in place of the form field’s attribute picker when the entity type this form is about has no attribute a participant could answer. "This type" is that node or edge type.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.formFieldV.defaultMessage: The attribute each answer is recorded in. Only attributes a form can collect are listed: a position or a location is written by the canvas, not answered.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.formFieldV.description: Guidance under the form field’s attribute picker, saying why some of the codebook’s attributes are missing from it.
Label of the picker naming the codebook attribute one form field records its answer in.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.formFieldV.defaultMessage: Choose the attribute this field records.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.formFieldV.description: Refusal shown under the form field’s attribute picker when the researcher saves a field without choosing one.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.freeDrawHi.defaultMessage: The participant can draw freehand annotations over the canvas, and erase them again.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.freeDrawLa.description: Label of the switch letting the participant draw freehand over the canvas.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.hullEmpty.defaultMessage: This type has no attributes with a fixed set of values, so there is nothing to group nodes by.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.hullEmpty.description: Shown in place of the composer grouping-attribute picker when the node type this stage is about has no categorical attribute the stage may take. "This type" is that node type.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.hullHint.defaultMessage: Nodes sharing a value of this attribute are drawn inside a shaded outline. The participant sets those values on the canvas, so this attribute is written without the codebook checking it.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.hullHint.description: Guidance under the composer grouping-attribute picker, warning that values written this way bypass the codebook’s validation rules.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.hullLabel.description: Label of the picker naming the codebook attribute a Network Composer stage draws shared outlines around nodes by. A categorical attribute holds one or more of a fixed set of values.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.inputContr.description: Researcher-facing name of the input control offering two named answers side by side. The words on the two buttons are the attribute’s own and default to Yes and No.
Researcher-facing name of the input control offering a set of options of which the participant may pick any number. The dash separates the control from what it allows.
Researcher-facing name of the input control the participant chooses a calendar date with.
Researcher-facing name of the input control offering a run of ordered, labelled steps between two extremes. Likert is a surname and is not translated.
Researcher-facing name of the input control that accepts a number only.
Researcher-facing name of the input control offering a set of options of which the participant may pick exactly one. The dash separates the control from what it allows.
Researcher-facing name of the input control the participant chooses a date with, measured from a fixed point rather than from the calendar — "three weeks ago" rather than a date.
Researcher-facing name of the input control that is one line the participant types into.
Researcher-facing name of the input control that is a box of several lines the participant types into.
Researcher-facing name of the input control that is a single switch the participant turns on or off.
Researcher-facing name of the input control offering a row of buttons the participant switches on and off independently. The dash separates the control from what it allows.
Researcher-facing name of the input control that is a slider the participant moves between two ends.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.layoutMode.defaultMessage: Positions nodes when the stage first opens by simulating physical forces such as attraction and repulsion. The participant can pause and resume the simulation, and reposition nodes by hand while it is paused.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.layoutMode.description: Says what the participant sees in automatic layout mode. A stage is one step of an interview; the simulation runs on the canvas while the participant watches.
Name of the choice where the stage arranges the nodes itself before the participant touches them. Offered as one of two cards; the sentence under it is layoutModeAutomaticDescription.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.layoutMode.defaultMessage: How the stage arranges nodes before the participant moves any of them.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.layoutMode.description: Label of the control choosing between manual and automatic node layout.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.layoutMode.defaultMessage: Places all nodes in a "bucket" at the bottom of the screen, from which the participant drags each one to where they want it.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.layoutMode.description: Says what the participant sees in manual layout mode. The "bucket" is the holding area at the foot of the canvas that unplaced nodes wait in; the quotation marks are in the English because it is a nickname for that area rather than a formal name.

Name of the choice where the stage does not arrange nodes at all and the participant places every one of them by hand. Offered as one of two cards; the sentence under it is layoutModeManualDescription.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.nodeFormAd.description: Button that opens the dialog for adding one more question to the node form. Whole rather than a generic "Add", because the same stage editor shows a connection list beside it and the two would otherwise be indistinguishable to anyone navigating by a list of buttons.
Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to add one more question to the node form.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.nodeFormCl.description: Button that confirms switching off the node form and discarding it.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.nodeFormCl.defaultMessage: Every field you have added to it will be removed, and the panel that opens when a participant selects a node will have nothing to ask.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.nodeFormCl.description: Body of the confirmation shown before the node form is switched off, saying what is lost. A field is one question the form asks; a node is one person or thing in the participant’s network.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.nodeFormCl.defaultMessage: This will delete the node form
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.nodeFormCl.description: Title of the confirmation shown before a researcher switches off the form a Network Composer stage asks about each node. Switching it off discards the form, which is why it is confirmed.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.nodeFormDe.defaultMessage: Optionally let the participant fill in more about each node after they have added it.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.nodeFormDe.description: Description of the node-attributes section, which is a capability the researcher can leave switched off.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.nodeFormEd.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to change a question the node form already asks.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.nodeFormEm.defaultMessage: No node attributes yet. Create one to ask the participant something about each node.
protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.nodeFormEm.description: Shown in place of the node form’s list of fields while it asks nothing yet.

protocolBuilder.networkCanvas.nodeFormFi.description: What one row of the node form’s list is called inside things said ABOUT it — "Edit node attribute field", "Remove this node attribute field?" — so it is lower case and singular. Qualified by "node" because the same stage editor shows a connection list beside it.
